title: Levers, pulleys and gears
examples: What is the difference between a lever and a pulley?
How do gears help us move things?
Can you show me an example of mechanical advantage?

explain.say: Today we are learning about simple machines. These are basic tools that make work easier.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: pulleys. Look at the fixed pulley, the movable pulley and the rope. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
A lever uses a rigid bar and a pivot point. This pivot point is called the fulcrum.
The effort is the force you apply to the machine. The load is the weight or force you are trying to move.

draw.text: Effort vs Load: Force Applied vs Moved

explain.say: Mechanical advantage tells us how much easier the machine makes the work. It is the ratio of load to effort.
Pulleys change the direction of force or reduce the effort needed. A single fixed pulley just changes direction.
Gears use interlocking to transfer motion and change speed or torque. A larger gear turning a smaller one spins faster.

faq.q: Why do we need to study simple machines?
faq.a: Simple machines help us do hard work with less effort. They are the basic principles behind many tools we use every day.
asks: What is the purpose of these machines?
How do these tools make things easier?

faq.q: Is a pulley always better than a lever?
faq.a: No, they are different tools for different jobs. A pulley is best for changing direction, while a lever is good for multiplying force.
asks: Which machine is better for lifting?
Can I use a pulley instead of a lever?

faq.q: How do I calculate mechanical advantage correctly?
faq.a: You find it by dividing the load you lift by the effort you use. Remember to keep your units consistent for an accurate answer.
asks: What is the formula for mechanical advantage?
Do I divide the effort by the load?

faq.q: Do gears always make things go faster?
faq.a: Not always. If the gear ratio is high, it can increase the force but decrease the speed. It depends on the size difference.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fixed and a movable pulley?
faq.a: A fixed pulley only changes the direction of the pull. A movable pulley supports the load and helps reduce the effort needed.
asks: What is the difference between the two pulley types?
Which pulley helps lift something heavier?

facts: A lever requires a fulcrum to work correctly.
Mechanical advantage is the ratio of load to effort.
Pulleys can change the direction of the applied force.
In gears, a smaller gear connected to a larger one spins faster.

quiz.say: A wheelbarrow uses a lever. If you lift a 50 newton load with a 10 newton effort, what is the mechanical advantage?
quiz.why: Mechanical advantage is calculated by dividing the load by the effort, so 50 divided by 10 equals 5.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you subtracted the load from the effort, which is not how mechanical advantage is calculated.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you added the load and the effort together instead of dividing them.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only used the effort value and ignored the load entirely.

quiz.say: If you use a single fixed pulley to lift a bucket, what does the pulley primarily change?
quiz.why: A fixed pulley redirects the force so you can pull down while lifting up, making it easier to grip.

wrong.1: The pulley does not change the actual weight of the bucket, only how you pull it.
wrong.2: A single fixed pulley does not reduce the effort; it only changes the direction.
wrong.3: While it relates to MA, its primary function is direction change, not force multiplication.

quiz.say: In a gear system, if a large gear turns a small gear, what happens to the speed?
quiz.why: When a large gear drives a smaller gear, the smaller gear must spin at a higher rate to keep up with the connection.

wrong.0: The gears are designed to work together; they will transfer motion efficiently.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because the smaller gear has fewer teeth and must spin more times to match the larger gear's rotation.
wrong.3: The speed will change because the gear sizes are different, which changes the ratio.
